data_schema.title: USDA Directive Extraction Schema v2.1 (DR/DM)
data_schema.description: Extracts metadata and structured policy statements from 3000 series USDA Departmental Regulation (DR) or Departmental Manual (DM). Governing rules: (1) Any field described as verbatim must be copied character-for-character from the source document. Never paraphrase, merge, abbreviate, summarize, or insert ellipses. (2) Do not infer. If the source does not support an optional field, leave the field out entirely. Never return an empty string or a guess. (3) Only the label fields in policy_statements (statement_kind, statement_function, modal_use, normative_force, actor_basis) are interpretations. Every other field is quoted or copied from the document.

document_type.description: Type of document as printed in the header, such as 'Departmental Regulation' or 'Departmental Manual'.

issuing_organization.description: Organization issuing the document, verbatim from the header.

issuing_location.description: Location of the issuing organization, verbatim from the header.

regulation_number.description: Official document number from the header, verbatim, for example 'DR 3105-001'.

subject.description: Subject or title of the document, verbatim from the header.

issue_date.description: Issue date from the header, as written.

expiration_date.description: Expiration date from the header, as written. Leave out if none is printed.

opi.description: Office of Primary Interest (OPI) from the header, verbatim.

supersedes.description: The prior document this document supersedes. Take all values from the supersession paragraph in the body (usually under Special Instructions/Cancellations), NOT from the header. Leave the whole object out if the document supersedes nothing.

document_number.description: Number of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph. If it is identical to this document's own number, still copy it from the supersession paragraph, not the header.

document_title.description: Title of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

document_date.description: Date of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

scope.description: The text of the Scope section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Scope section.

purpose.description: The text of the Purpose section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Purpose section.

inquiries.description: Contact information from the Inquiries section. Leave out any property the document does not state; never return an empty string.

office.description: Office or division named for inquiries, verbatim. Leave out if the document names no office.

email.description: Email address given for inquiries, verbatim, without trailing punctuation. Leave out if none is given.

table_of_contents.description: Top-level entries of the printed table of contents, in order, including appendices. Return an empty list if the document prints no table of contents.

section_number.description: Section or appendix identifier as printed, for example '1.' or 'Appendix A'.

section_title.description: Section or appendix title as printed in the table of contents.

page.description: Page number exactly as printed in the table of contents, for example '2' or 'A-1'. Copy it even if the section actually starts on a different page. Leave out if no page number is printed.

actors.description: Registry of every distinct entity that the policy text names in an acting role. One entry per entity. Include every entity used as actor_name in policy_statements. Also include entities the document names in a role without being directed to act (mark those mentioned_only). Documents (bylaws, regulations, directives) are NEVER actors and must not appear here. Return an empty list if the document names no actors.

name.description: The entity's name exactly as written in the policy text, without a leading article ('the') and without a possessive. Keep a compound name intact if the document writes it as one phrase, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'. This is the join key used by actor_name in policy_statements, so spell it identically there.

components.description: ONLY for a name that joins separate entities with commas or 'and' (for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices' gives 'USDA Mission Areas', 'agencies', 'staff offices'). NEVER split a job title from the organization that qualifies it ('Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General' is ONE position), and never split an organization name from the position it modifies ('Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO)' is ONE group). Each component is a verbatim substring of the name. Leave out for single entities.

items.description: One verbatim component of a compound actor name.

actor_type.description: Kind of entity. Use exactly one of: position (a job title, singular or plural, for example 'USDA CIO' or 'Mission Area Assistant CIOs'), office (an organizational unit, for example 'OCIO Executive Secretariat'), council_or_body (a council, committee, board, or similar body), group (a category of organizations or units, not job titles, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'), external_entity (an entity outside the document's authority), program_or_system (an IT initiative, system, program, or project that the document says must act or conform).

binding_status.description: bound_by_this_document: the document directs, permits, or assigns a function or role to this entity and has authority over it. mentioned_only: the document names the entity but cannot or does not impose anything on it (for example a council or agency outside USDA that the document says a USDA body partners with).

policy_statements.description: Structured statements from the numbered body sections only (not the table of contents, not the appendices). RULES. (a) SENTENCES: emit one statement per sentence. If a paragraph has more than one sentence, give each its own statement with ids suffixed .s1, .s2, and so on. Abbreviations and legal citations ('U.S.C.', 'CFR', '§', 'et seq.') do not end a sentence. (b) LISTS: when text introduces a list (usually ends with a colon, for example 'The USDA CIO will:'), emit the introducing text as one statement with statement_kind 'lead_in', and emit EVERY item of the list as its own statement with statement_kind 'list_item' and parent_statement_id set to the id of the lead_in. Never skip list items, including lists of legal authorities. For a list inside a list, parent_statement_id is the immediate parent. (c) NEVER merge text from different sentences, paragraphs, or list items into one statement. (d) Copy text exactly; do not summarize. (e) PRONOUNS: when a sentence's subject is a pronoun ('It', 'Its', 'They') that refers to a named actor in the preceding sentence, resolve it: set actor_name to that actor and actor_basis to resolved_from_prior_sentence. (f) DOCUMENT AS SUBJECT: when the grammatical subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'), leave actor_name out; the entities the document acts on belong in target.

statement_id.description: Printed numbering path of the statement: section number, then paragraph letter, then item number in parentheses, for example '1', '3.a', '5.d.s2', '6.a(1)'. Add '.sN' only when a paragraph contains more than one sentence. Must be unique within the document.

statement_kind.description: standalone: a complete sentence that stands on its own. lead_in: text that introduces a list and is incomplete without its items. list_item: a list item that completes its lead_in.

parent_statement_id.description: Include ONLY when statement_kind is list_item: the statement_id of its immediate lead_in. For every other statement leave this field out entirely; never return an empty string.

section_number.description: Number of the section containing the statement, digits only, for example '6'.

section_title.description: Title of the section containing the statement, as shown in the table of contents, for example 'Roles and Responsibilities'.

source_text.description: VERBATIM text of this one sentence or list item exactly as printed, including trailing punctuation such as ':' or ';' and including any list-ending words such as 'and'. No paraphrase, no ellipses, no text from any other statement. For a list_item, give only the item's own text, not the lead_in.

statement_function.description: What the statement does. obligation: a required action or compliance requirement on an actor. responsibility: a standing duty or function assigned to an actor, including present-tense descriptions of what a body does. role_designation: assigns an entity to a role, for example membership or voting status. authority: names a legal source of authority or a grant of authority. scope: states what or whom the document applies to. purpose: states why the document or a body exists. definition: defines a term. condition: states a standalone triggering condition. exception: carves out an exception. savings_clause: states that the document does not displace existing authorities or delegations. effectivity: states when the document takes effect or how long it lasts. supersession: states that the document replaces another. classification_rule: states a rule that classifies something or applies a requirement when a status is met. reference: points to another document or location. inquiry: tells who may be contacted. container: use for every lead_in statement. other: none of the above.

modal_verb.description: The modal word or phrase of the statement's MAIN clause, exactly as written, for example 'will', 'can', 'may', 'must', 'shall', 'must not'. Ignore modals inside relative or subordinate clauses (for 'advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments', the 'may' is not the statement's modal). For a list_item whose own text has no modal, copy the modal from its lead_in. Leave out if the main clause has no modal.

modal_use.description: deontic: the main-clause modal directs, permits, or prohibits action by an actor (for example 'The Deputy CIO will serve', 'can direct questions'). predictive: the modal only states what will happen or remain true (for example 'It will remain in effect until superseded'). none: the main clause has no modal.

normative_force.description: mandatory: deontic 'will', 'shall', or 'must' directing an actor to act or to serve in a role. prohibitive: deontic 'must not', 'shall not', or 'may not'. permissive: deontic 'may' or 'can'. assigned: a present-tense statement with no deontic modal that assigns or describes a function, duty, or role of a named actor (for example 'The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on...', 'It assesses the needs of...'); use it only when actor_name is present, and never for purpose statements. descriptive: everything else with no deontic force, including purpose, scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, references, authorities, definitions, and statements about the document itself or about other documents. not_applicable: use for every lead_in; its force is carried by its list_items.

actor_name.description: The entity directed to act, permitted to act, or assigned a function or role by this statement, spelled exactly as in the matching actors[].name. It must appear in source_text or in the lead_in's text (leading article removed); for a resolved pronoun, copy it from the antecedent sentence. Leave out when the statement binds no actor: scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, statements about documents (including bylaws), and any statement whose subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'). Never supply an actor that is not stated in the text or resolvable from the preceding sentence. Always leave out for lead_in statements.

actor_basis.description: Include ONLY when actor_name is present; otherwise leave this field out entirely. explicit_in_statement: the actor appears in this statement's own source_text. inherited_from_lead_in: the actor appears only in the lead_in that this list_item completes. resolved_from_prior_sentence: the subject is a pronoun resolved to the actor named in the preceding sentence.

target.description: VERBATIM phrase naming what the action is directed at or what the statement applies to, starting at the first word after any leading article ('a', 'an', 'the'). For a role_designation, the body or unit the role is within (for example 'CIO Council'). Leave out if none.

resulting_status.description: VERBATIM phrase naming the status or role that a role_designation or classification_rule confers, for example 'voting member' or 'advisory (non-voting) members'. Leave out for other statements.

conditions.description: VERBATIM phrases that restrict when or to what the statement applies, for example 'that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives'. Do NOT treat a non-restrictive descriptive phrase set off by commas (for example 'appointed by the USDA CIO' in 'The Secretariat, appointed by the USDA CIO, will serve') as a condition. Leave out if there are none.

items.description: One verbatim condition phrase copied from source_text.

cross_references.description: Other documents, laws, or regulations cited in source_text, each copied verbatim as ONE entry per cited authority, including its code citation (for example 'The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.' is one entry; for a list_item that is just a citation, the entry is the item text without the trailing ';' or 'and'). Never add a separate entry for a title that is part of the same citation (the words 'Chief Information Officer' after '7 CFR § 2.32'). Never list generic categories such as 'law' or 'Federal regulation'. Leave out if none.

acronyms.description: Acronyms and abbreviations listed in the acronym appendix, one entry per row, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no acronym appendix.

acronym.description: Acronym or abbreviation exactly as printed.

authorities_and_references.description: Entries of the Authorities and References appendix, one per entry, each copied verbatim, including any date, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no such appendix.

items.description: One appendix entry exactly as printed, joined across line breaks.

policy_statements.source_text: The United States Department of Agriculture’s (USDA) Agriculture Learning (AgLearn) System is a strategic component of USDA’s eGovernment initiative and enterprise architecture providing a common learning management system and related services.
AgLearn contributes to meeting the goals and objectives outlined in USDA Strategic Plan, FY 2018-2022, Goal 1, Objectives 1.1 and 1.2.
policy_statements.target: goals and objectives outlined in USDA Strategic Plan, FY 2018-2022, Goal 1, Objectives 1.1 and 1.2
cross_references: USDA Strategic Plan, FY 2018-2022, Goal 1, Objectives 1.1 and 1.2

policy_statements.source_text: This Departmental Regulation (DR) documents USDA’s AgLearn policy, framework, roles, and responsibilities.
Policies in this DR are defined around Federal authorities to develop and implement training policies as well as USDA’s enterprise architecture and investment strategies.
This DR applies to all USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices.
policy_statements.target: all USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: This DR supersedes DR 3620-001, USDA eLearning Services, Courseware and Content, dated October 29, 2004.
cross_references: DR 3620-001, USDA eLearning Services, Courseware and Content, dated October 29, 2004

policy_statements.source_text: AgLearn services provide USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices with a consolidated, cost effective, enterprisewide learning service for employees, contractors, partners, volunteers, affiliates, students, and customers.
policy_statements.target: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: AgLearn provides USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices and their customers with a one-stop access to training products and services at reduced overall costs.
policy_statements.target: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices and their customers

policy_statements.source_text: AgLearn is a component within the Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO).
policy_statements.target: Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO)

policy_statements.source_text: AgLearn supports the E-Government Act of 2002, 44 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 3501, by promoting the use of the internet and emerging technologies within Government, reducing costs and burdens for Government, promoting more informed decision making, and providing access to high-quality Government information and services across multiple channels.
cross_references: E-Government Act of 2002, 44 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 3501

policy_statements.source_text: Thus, making the Federal Government more transparent and accountable.

AgLearn supports the Strategic Human Capital Management Framework prescribed in 5 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) 250, Subpart B and USDA’s human capital strategic efforts as a means to attract, develop, and retain a high-performing and diverse workforce, as well as close mission critical skill gaps.
cross_references: 5 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) 250, Subpart B

policy_statements.source_text: The Director of AgLearn will coordinate with the Office of Human Resources Management (OHRM) when procuring training delivery systems and online courseware libraries.
conditions: when procuring training delivery systems and online courseware libraries

policy_statements.source_text: Specifically, the following apply to the purchase of online training and related services:
Mission Areas, agency and staff office AgLearn Lead Administrators are the liaisons to OHRM and OCIO for the purchase of courseware libraries.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agency and staff office AgLearn Lead Administrators

policy_statements.source_text: All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices must purchase online courseware libraries through the purchasing authority of the Director of AgLearn.
policy_statements.actor_name: All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Purchase of online courseware libraries from other sources may be made only with the written approval of the Director, OHRM, and the USDA Chief Information Officer (CIO).
conditions: only with the written approval of the Director, OHRM, and the USDA Chief Information Officer (CIO)

policy_statements.source_text: Such approval may be granted only in those instances where courses desired by Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices are not available through AgLearn.
conditions: only in those instances where courses desired by Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices are not available through AgLearn

policy_statements.source_text: Procurement offices will not process requests or actions for online courseware or Learning Management Systems (LMS) unless the action is accompanied by written approval from the Director, OHRM, and the CIO.
policy_statements.target: requests or actions for online courseware or Learning Management Systems (LMS)
conditions: unless the action is accompanied by written approval from the Director, OHRM, and the CIO

policy_statements.source_text: The Director of AgLearn will be informed and consulted with when any USDA organization purchases or deploys any type of electronic training delivery system or service.
conditions: when any USDA organization purchases or deploys any type of electronic training delivery system or service

policy_statements.source_text: AgLearn is the official system of record for training and contains training history of USDA employees, contractors, partners, political appointees, volunteers, affiliates, students, and customers.
policy_statements.resulting_status: official system of record for training

policy_statements.source_text: As stated in Reporting, 5 CFR § 410.601 (c), all Federal Agencies are required to establish a schedule of training records.
USDA adheres to the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA), General Records Schedule 2.6.
policy_statements.target: National Archives and Records Administration (NARA), General Records Schedule 2.6
cross_references: National Archives and Records Administration (NARA), General Records Schedule 2.6

policy_statements.source_text: Training records at USDA will be disposed of after 6 years.
conditions: after 6 years

policy_statements.source_text: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices may submit a request to the Director of AgLearn to retain training records longer than the Disposition Authority stated on the NARA schedule of Governmentwide records if the records are required for business use.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: if the records are required for business use

policy_statements.source_text: All USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will have access to AgLearn.
policy_statements.actor_name: All USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: AgLearn provides the mechanism to deliver, track, and record training, examinations, and surveys completed by USDA employees, partners, and contract staff.
policy_statements.target: training, examinations, and surveys completed by USDA employees, partners, and contract staff

policy_statements.source_text: Available through the internet and fully integrated with USDA eAuthentication service, it is a secure service that is accessible in and outside of USDA and is available 24 hours each day.

All Federal Agencies, as stated in Reporting, 5 CFR § 410.601 (a), are required to capture and record training records, expenditures, and activities and submit to Office of Personnel Management’s (OPM) Data, Analysis & Documentation, Enterprise Human Resources Integration (EHRI) data warehouse.
cross_references: Office of Personnel Management’s (OPM) Data, Analysis & Documentation, Enterprise Human Resources Integration

policy_statements.source_text: AgLearn follows OPM’s Data, Analysis & Documentation, Data Policy & Guidance, Guide to Human Resource Reporting when reporting all completed training activities to EHRI.
policy_statements.target: OPM’s Data, Analysis & Documentation, Data Policy & Guidance, Guide to Human Resource Reporting
conditions: when reporting all completed training activities to EHRI
cross_references: OPM’s Data, Analysis & Documentation, Data Policy & Guidance, Guide to Human Resource Reporting

policy_statements.source_text: All AgLearn Leads and Administrators are to ensure all employee training activities are captured in AgLearn.
AgLearn users have access to the OPM Standard Form (SF) 182, Authorization, Agreement and Certification of Training form.
policy_statements.target: OPM Standard Form (SF) 182, Authorization, Agreement and Certification of Training form
cross_references: OPM Standard Form (SF) 182, Authorization, Agreement and Certification of Training

policy_statements.source_text: This is a Governmentwide training form used to request, approve, and certify completion of training activities.
The SF-182 includes the mandatory training data elements USDA must report to OPM.
As an official USDA corporate system, any course content on AgLearn will be training that is appropriate to be documented as part of an individual’s USDA training record.
policy_statements.resulting_status: training that is appropriate to be documented as part of an individual’s USDA training record

policy_statements.source_text: Content may include online training, classroom training, webinars, examinations, surveys, handbooks, books, and videos.
Custom developed courses or commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) courseware must meet specific industry standards to work properly on AgLearn.
policy_statements.actor_name: Custom developed courses or commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) courseware

policy_statements.source_text: These are currently Aviation Industry Computer-Based Training Committee (AICC) or Shareable Content Object Reference Model (SCORM) standards.
Mission Areas, agency and staff office Course Owners will review all courses for relevancy and content 2 years after its posting date thereafter.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agency and staff office Course Owners
conditions: 2 years after its posting date thereafter

policy_statements.source_text: The course owners must review courses every 2 years thereafter.
conditions: every 2 years thereafter

policy_statements.source_text: The Director of AgLearn retains the right to remove courses at his or her discretion and will notify the course owner immediately if course removal occurs.
conditions: if course removal occurs

policy_statements.source_text: The Director of AgLearn sets an end-of-life date on all online courses.
The default end-of-life date is 5 years from the date of the course publication unless a different date is requested at the time of submission.
conditions: unless a different date is requested at the time of submission

policy_statements.source_text: All USDA online courses, videos, and books must adhere to the policies set forth in Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 (29 U.S.C. § 794d).
policy_statements.actor_name: All USDA online courses, videos, and books
policy_statements.target: policies set forth in Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 (29 U.S.C. § 794d)
cross_references: Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 (29 U.S.C. § 794d)

policy_statements.source_text: Any online course, video, or book that is not Section 508 compliant is subject to removal from AgLearn.
policy_statements.target: Any online course, video, or book that is not Section 508 compliant
conditions: that is not Section 508 compliant

policy_statements.source_text: For more information, refer to DR 4030-001, Section 508 Program.
USDA requires all supervisors, managers, and executives to complete a 360-degree assessment at least every 3 years.
conditions: at least every 3 years

policy_statements.source_text: Supervisors, managers, and executives should use AgLearn to complete 360-degree assessments to meet this requirement in DR 4040-412-001, Leadership Competency Framework and Assessments.
cross_references: DR 4040-412-001, Leadership Competency Framework and Assessments

policy_statements.source_text: Content available through AgLearn may be made available to users of AgLearn, including the public or restricted to specific groups of employees or customers.
policy_statements.target: users of AgLearn, including the public or restricted to specific groups of employees or customers

policy_statements.source_text: The owner of the content or learning activity typically makes access decisions.
policy_statements.actor_name: owner of the content or learning activity

policy_statements.source_text: USDA employees have access to an online Individual Develop Plan (IDP) or Executive Development Plan (EDP) through AgLearn.
policy_statements.target: online Individual Develop Plan (IDP) or Executive Development Plan (EDP)

policy_statements.source_text: USDA requires the following employees to complete an IDP:
Presidential Management Fellows,
Senior Executive Service Candidate Development Program participants,
policy_statements.target: Senior Executive Service Candidate Development Program participants

policy_statements.source_text: all non-bargaining unit employees, and
any employee who requests an IDP.
policy_statements.target: any employee who requests an IDP
conditions: who requests an IDP

policy_statements.source_text: All Senior Executives, Senior Level, Scientific, and Senior Science and Technology Services groups are required to complete an EDP.
policy_statements.actor_name: All Senior Executives, Senior Level, Scientific, and Senior Science and Technology Services groups

policy_statements.source_text: For more information on IDPs, refer to DR 4040-410, Creating Individual Development Plans (IDP).
For more information on EDPs, refer to DR 4740-003, Executive Continual Learning Program.
USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will ensure any custom online content they have developed complies with published AgLearn standards.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
policy_statements.target: any custom online content they have developed
conditions: they have developed

policy_statements.source_text: Source data is processed through the Identity, Credential, and Access Management (ICAM) and Enterprise Entitlement Management System (EEMS).
This automated provisioning of user data is completed daily.
All user data will be processed in AgLearn through this enterprise solution.
Every user type in AgLearn is required to use an eAuthentication-managed account for access to AgLearn.

Administrative roles are granted as part of the authoritative data source enforcement and Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014 (FISMA), 44 U.S.C. § 3551, compliant access control practices.
cross_references: Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014 (FISMA), 44 U.S.C. § 3551

policy_statements.source_text: An administrator may never change a user’s account status in AgLearn.
All user account changes related to active status or disabled status must be completed at the authoritative data source (e.g., the USDA Human Resources (HR) systems).
policy_statements.target: All user account changes related to active status or disabled status

policy_statements.source_text: USDA’s non-Federal users have limited access to AgLearn.
All contractors, volunteers, and partners are required to complete annual information security awareness training as described in DR 3545-001, Information Security Awareness and Training Policy.
cross_references: DR 3545-001, Information Security Awareness and Training Policy

policy_statements.source_text: Some course content in AgLearn is not available to contractors.

Contractor organizations should provide fully trained employees to perform the work and offer continual learning and development for employees to maintain and improve their knowledge and skills outside of AgLearn.
The USDA CIO will:
Provide leadership for overall technical and operational direction of AgLearn; and

Provide written approval of the purchase of online courseware libraries from other sources, in coordination with the Director of AgLearn and the Director of OHRM, in those instances where courses desired by Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices are not available through AgLearn as stated in Section 5b of this DR.
policy_statements.target: purchase of online courseware libraries from other sources
conditions: in those instances where courses desired by Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices are not available through AgLearn

policy_statements.source_text: The Director of OHRM will:
Provide the overall leadership for USDA’s learning and development strategy;

Provide written approval of the purchase of online courseware libraries from other sources, in coordination with the CIO and the Director of AgLearn, in those instances where courses desired by Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices are not available through AgLearn as stated in Section 5b of this DR;
policy_statements.target: purchase of online courseware libraries from other sources
conditions: in those instances where courses desired by Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices are not available through AgLearn

policy_statements.source_text: Provide leadership for incorporating AgLearn services into the training and human resource operations at USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices.
Specific areas may include developing and issuing guidance about the use of AgLearn for training requests, IDPs, EDP, SF-182s, training records, and 360-degree competency assessments.
The Director of AgLearn will:
Provide strategic, technical, and operational leadership for AgLearn;
Be informed and consulted with when any USDA organization purchases or deploys any type of electronic training delivery asset or service;
conditions: when any USDA organization purchases or deploys any type of electronic training delivery asset or service

policy_statements.source_text: Coordinate with OHRM when procuring training delivery systems and online courseware libraries;
conditions: when procuring training delivery systems and online courseware libraries

policy_statements.source_text: Provide written approval of the purchase of online courseware libraries from other sources, in coordination with the CIO and the Director of OHRM, in those instances where courses desired by Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices are not available through AgLearn as stated in Section 5b of this DR;
policy_statements.target: purchase of online courseware libraries from other sources
conditions: in those instances where courses desired by Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices are not available through AgLearn

policy_statements.source_text: Set an end-of-life date on all online courses; and
Retain the right to remove courses at his/her discretion and will notify the course owner immediately if this occurs.
conditions: if this occurs

policy_statements.source_text: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office AgLearn Lead Administrators will:
Act as the liaison between their Mission Area, agency, or staff office and the Director of AgLearn as stated in Section 5a of this DR;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office AgLearn Lead Administrators
policy_statements.target: their Mission Area, agency, or staff office and the Director of AgLearn

extract_result.purpose:
a. The United States Department of Agriculture’s (USDA) Agriculture Learning (AgLearn) System is a strategic component of USDA’s eGovernment initiative and enterprise architecture providing a common learning management system and related services. AgLearn contributes to meeting the goals and objectives outlined in USDA Strategic Plan, FY 2018-2022, Goal 1, Objectives 1.1 and 1.2.
b. This Departmental Regulation (DR) documents USDA’s AgLearn policy, framework, roles, and responsibilities. Policies in this DR are defined around Federal authorities to develop and implement training policies as well as USDA’s enterprise architecture and investment strategies.

The United States Department of Agriculture’s (USDA) Agriculture Learning (AgLearn) System is a strategic component of USDA’s eGovernment initiative and enterprise architecture providing a common learning management system and related services.
AgLearn contributes to meeting the goals and objectives outlined *in  USDA Strategic Plan, FY 2018-2022, Goal 1, Objectives 1.1 and 1.2
goals and objectives outlined *in  USDA Strategic Plan, FY 2018-2022, Goal 1, Objectives 1.1 and 1.2

This Departmental Regulation (DR) documents USDA’s AgLearn policy, framework, roles, and responsibilities.
Policies in this DR are defined around Federal authorities to develop and implement training policies as well as USDA’s enterprise architecture and investment strategies.
This DR applies to all USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices.
all USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
This DR supersedes DR 3620-001, *USDA eLearning Services, Courseware and Content*, dated October 29, 2004
DR 3620-001, *USDA eLearning Services, Courseware and Content*, dated October 29, 2004

AgLearn services provide USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices with a consolidated, cost effective, enterprisewide learning service for employees, contractors, partners, volunteers, affiliates, students, and customers.
AgLearn provides USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices and their customers with a one-stop access to training products and services at reduced overall costs.
USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices and their customers
AgLearn is a component within the Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO).
Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO)

b. AgLearn supports the *E-Government Act of 2002*, 44  United States Code (U.S.C.) § 3501 , by promoting the use of the internet and emerging technologies within Government, reducing costs and burdens for Government, promoting more informed decision making, and providing access to high-quality Government information and services across multiple channels. Thus, making the Federal Government more transparent and accountable.
Thus, making the Federal Government more transparent and accountable.

AgLearn supports the Strategic Human Capital Management Framework prescribed in  5 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) 250, Subpart B  and USDA’s human capital strategic efforts as a means to attract, develop, and retain a high-performing and diverse workforce, as well as close mission critical skill gaps.
5 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) 250, Subpart B

a. AgLearn is the official system of record for training and contains training history of USDA employees, contractors, partners, political appointees, volunteers, affiliates, students, and customers. As stated in *Reporting*,  5 CFR § 410.601 (c) , all Federal Agencies are required to establish a schedule of training records. USDA adheres to the  National Archives and Records Administration (NARA), General Records Schedule 2.6 . Training records at USDA will be disposed of after 6 years. Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices may submit a request to the Director of AgLearn to retain training records longer than the Disposition Authority stated on the NARA schedule of Governmentwide records if the records are required for business use.

Available through the internet and fully integrated with USDA eAuthentication service, it is a secure service that is accessible in and outside of USDA and is available 24 hours each day.

c. All Federal Agencies, as stated in *Reporting*,  5 CFR § 410.601 (a) , are required to capture and record training records, expenditures, and activities and submit to Office of Personnel Management’s (OPM)  *Data, Analysis & Documentation, Enterprise Human Resources Integration*  (EHRI) data warehouse. AgLearn follows OPM’s  *Data, Analysis & Documentation, Data Policy & Guidance, Guide to Human Resource Reporting*  when reporting all completed training activities to EHRI. All AgLearn Leads and Administrators are to ensure all employee training activities are captured in AgLearn.
